limitations_and_boundaries: Mosaic-seq relies on antibiotic selection, limiting application to proliferating cells.
Mosaic-seq cannot distinguish primary enhancer targets from downstream secondary effects.
Due to detection limits of scRNA-seq, applying Mosaic-seq to enhancers regulating low-expression genes may require more sequencing depth or more cells.
Mosaic-seq is about 83 times more expensive than high-throughput reporter assays, limiting genome-wide application.
It is unknown whether KRAB is a universal repressor of all enhancers, potentially leading to false negatives.

missed_core_items.description: The number of constituent enhancers (71) and super-enhancers (15) analyzed, and the total number of single-cell transcriptomes (12,444) with detectable sgRNA barcodes.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Applying Mosaic-seq to 71 constituent enhancers from 15 super-enhancers, our analysis of 51,448 sgRNA-induced transcriptomes finds that only a small number of constituents are major effectors of target gene expression.

missed_core_items.description: The finding that only a small number of constituent enhancers are major effectors of target gene expression, with most constituents showing no detectable changes when repressed individually.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Overall, we find that these constituents have a widely variable effect on gene expression when averaged across cells, ranging from 18.0% to 88.9%, with a median of 42.3%. In contrast, most constituents tested elicit no detectable changes in expression, suggesting that they only contribute weakly to gene expression, at least when studied in isolation with KRAB.

missed_core_items.description: The validation that non-hit enhancers were specifically modified by H3K9me3 recruitment, confirming effective targeting.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Fourth, even for enhancers not significantly linked to gene expression changes, chromatin analysis indicates that they were specifically modified by sgRNA-mediated recruitment of H3K9me3 (Figures 5D and S4C).

missed_core_items.description: The cost and time savings of Mosaic-seq compared to traditional methods (4X cost, 3.5X time).
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: We estimate that, to examine 100 enhancers, the current prototype of Mosaic-seq represents a significant savings in cost (~4X) and time (~3.5X) compared to traditional methods (Table S8).

missed_core_items.description: The limitation that Mosaic-seq cannot distinguish primary enhancer targets from downstream secondary effects.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: Also, as with the low-throughput application of CRISPRi to repress enhancers, Mosaic-seq cannot distinguish primary enhancer targets from downstream secondary effects.

missed_core_items.description: The limitation that Mosaic-seq is about 83 times more expensive than high-throughput reporter assays, limiting genome-wide application.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: In addition, Mosaic-seq is about 83 more expensive than high-throughput reporter assays, which will limit its genome-wide application to test all predicted enhancers until sequencing costs decrease.

missed_core_items.description: The limitation that it is unknown whether KRAB is a universal repressor of all enhancers, potentially leading to false negatives.
missed_core_items.source_excerpt: In its current application, Mosaic-seq relies on the KRAB repressor. As it is unknown whether KRAB is a universal repressor of all enhancers, it is possible that there are false negatives.

research_questions.statement: What is the functional activity of constituent enhancers within super-enhancers, and how do they combinatorially regulate gene expression?

provenance.text_excerpt: Together, these observations suggest that simultaneous repression of multiple weak constituents can robustly alter super-enhancer activity and that it does so in a manner that is significantly greater than the repression of individual constituents. These observations are consistent with a compensatory relationship between weaker enhancers.

claims.statement: Simultaneous repression of multiple weak constituent enhancers can robustly alter super-enhancer activity, consistent with a compensatory relationship.

provenance.text_excerpt: These results emphasize that features of the transcriptional machinery may be better indicators of enhancer activity than histone modifications.

claims.statement: Features of the transcriptional machinery, such as p300 and RNAPII binding, are better indicators of enhancer activity than histone modifications like H3K4me1 and H3K27ac.

provenance.text_excerpt: Our analysis indicates that the single-cell penetrance and contribution of enhancers is heterogeneous, and suggests that an enhancer's contribution to target gene expression in penetrant cells may not be directly proportional to its penetrance across a cell population.

claims.statement: Single-cell penetrance and contribution of enhancers are heterogeneous and can be decoupled.

experiments_or_tasks: For each of the 36 pairwise combinations of two sgRNAs (excluding HS2), a median of 154 cells were sequenced.
Mosaic-seq was performed at high viral titer using sgRNAs targeting ten constituents on TAD2 SE2, detecting an average of 2.8 sgRNAs per cell.
Single-cell penetrance analysis was performed to model enhancer activity.

methods.name: Mosaic-seq
methods.protocol_description: Combines single-cell RNA sequencing with CRISPRi (dCas9-KRAB) to repress enhancers and measure gene expression changes. sgRNA barcodes are used to identify perturbations in single cells.

methods.name: Single-cell penetrance analysis
methods.protocol_description: Statistical modeling over two parameters: single-cell penetrance (percentage of sgRNA-expressing cells with altered expression) and gene expression contribution (level of repression in those cells). Models are compared via likelihood to infer most consistent parameters.
